title: Effectivity of formal homomorphisms from a split diagonalizable group
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] for which the canonical map $A\to\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/\mathfrak m^n$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $A_n=A/\mathfrak m^n$ and $S_n=\operatorname{Spec}A_n$. An $S$-group scheme is an $S$-scheme with multiplication, identity section and inverse satisfying the associativity, unit and inverse diagrams; a homomorphism preserves these three operations. For a finitely generated additive abelian group $M$, let $A[M]$ be the free $A$-module on symbols $e_m$, with $e_me_n=e_{m+n}$, unit $e_0$, comultiplication $e_m\mapsto e_m\otimes e_m$, counit $e_m\mapsto1$ and antipode $e_m\mapsto e_{-m}$. Write $D_A(M)=\operatorname{Spec}A[M]$ with the resulting group operations. Let $G\to S$ be an affine group scheme of finite type, meaning that $G=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ a finitely generated commutative $A$-algebra. Set $G_n=G\times_SS_n$ [def-pc-base-change]. The reduction map is a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{S\text{-}\mathrm{gp}}(D_A(M),G)\ \longrightarrow\ \varprojlim_{n\geq1}\operatorname{Hom}_{S_n\text{-}\mathrm{gp}}(D_{A_n}(M),G_n).$$
The set on the right consists of families $(u_n)_{n\geq1}$ such that the base change of $u_{n+1}$ along $A_{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow A_n$ is $u_n$; the displayed map takes a homomorphism to all its reductions. In particular every such compatible family is the reduction of a unique homomorphism defined over $A$. Smoothness of $G$ is not required.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes (2014), Theorem B.3.2(1), formula (B.3.1), printed p.288: the split-source instance. Its proof explicitly isolates the non-module-finite completion/tensor-product calculation. WANTED local archive; online statement and surrounding proof read. This is retained as a statement-only prerequisite.

proof.text: Write $C=A[M]$ and $C_n=A_n[M]$. The affine fibre-product formula gives $G_n=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_AA_n)$. The map $C\otimes_AA_n\to C_n$, $e_m\otimes a\mapsto ae_m$, has inverse $ae_m\mapsto e_m\otimes a$, extended additively over finite sums: they respect the bilinearity relations, multiplication and each of the three displayed group operations. For $G$, apply affine duality and the fibre-product formula to multiplication, identity and inverse to obtain $A$-algebra maps $\Delta_B:B\to B\otimes_AB$, $\epsilon_B:B\to A$ and $s_B:B\to B$. Applying the same functor to the diagrams says exactly that an $S$-group homomorphism $D_A(M)\to G$ corresponds to an $A$-algebra map $f:B\to C$ with $\Delta_C f=(f\otimes f)\Delta_B$, $\epsilon_C f=\epsilon_B$ and $s_C f=f s_B$. Tensor maps here are defined on pure tensors; the algebra tensor universal property constructs them. Thus the given family is equivalently a compatible family of $A$-algebra maps $f_n:B\to C_n$ satisfying these identities after reduction. This uses affine duality over $A$, not a Hopf-algebra assertion restricted to fields.

proof.text: For each $b\in B$ and $m\in M$, compatibility of $f_n$ makes the coefficient of $e_m$ in $f_n(b)$ a compatible sequence in $A_n$. Completeness gives a unique $a_m(b)\in A$ with these residues. Also, an element of $A$ whose residues all vanish is zero, by injectivity of the canonical completion map. For any set $J$ this detects equality of finite sums in $\bigoplus_{j\in J}A$ coefficient by coefficient. At this point $(a_m(b))_{m\in M}$ is merely a family of coefficients; finite support has not been assumed.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Theorem B.3.2(1), formula (B.3.1), printed p.288; agent proof of its split-source completion calculation, using only affine duality and the Noetherian maximal condition.

proof.text:
Fix $b$. A tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors, so write $\Delta_B(b)=\sum_{i=1}^r x_i\otimes y_i$. Set $\alpha_m=(a_m(x_i))_{i=1}^r\in A^r$ and define the linear form $\lambda_t:A^r\to A$ by $\lambda_t(z)=\sum_i z_i a_t(y_i)$. At level $n$ the comultiplication identity from Step 1 gives, by comparing the $(e_m\otimes e_t)$ coefficient,
$$\delta_{m,t}\,\overline{a_m(b)}=\sum_{i=1}^r\overline{a_m(x_i)}\,\overline{a_t(y_i)}.$$
Here $C_n\otimes_{A_n}C_n$ is free on $(e_m\otimes e_t)_{(m,t)\in M^2}$: the coefficient map on this tensor product is induced by the bilinear map sending two finite sums to the products of their coefficients, inverse to the map sending the $(m,t)$ basis vector to $e_m\otimes e_t$. All sums in this levelwise calculation are finite. As the displayed identity holds for every $n$, injectivity in Step 2 yields
$$\lambda_t(\alpha_m)=\delta_{m,t}a_m(b)\quad(m,t\in M).$$

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Theorem B.3.2(1), formula (B.3.1), printed p.288; agent proof of its split-source completion calculation, using only affine duality and the Noetherian maximal condition.

proof.text: Apply the maximal condition for submodules of a finite module over a Noetherian ring to $A^r$, generated by its $r$ standard basis vectors. Consider its nonempty set of submodules $N_F=\operatorname{span}_A\{\alpha_m:m\in F\}$ for finite subsets $F\subset M$, including $F=\varnothing$. There is a maximal such $N_F$. For each $m$, $N_F\subseteq N_{F\cup\{m\}}$, so maximality forces equality and $\alpha_m\in N_F$. If $t\notin F$, Step 3 gives $\lambda_t(\alpha_m)=0$ for all $m\in F$. Linearity then gives $a_t(b)=\lambda_t(\alpha_t)=0$. Hence $a_m(b)$ has finite support. This proves the required support bound for each $b$, using no finite-dimensional coalgebra assertion and no flatness hypothesis on $B$. The argument also works for $r=0$.

source.place: Agent finite-support argument for Conrad Theorem B.3.2(1), printed p.288; Stacks Tag 00IK, algebra.tex, lemma-Noetherian-basic, maximal/ascending-chain condition for submodules of a finite module.

proof.text: Define $f(b)=\sum_m a_m(b)e_m\in C$, which is a finite sum by Step 4. Its reduction to $C_n$ is $f_n(b)$: both have the same coefficient at every $m$. For $b,b'\in B$ and $a\in A$, the differences $f(b+b')-f(b)-f(b')$, $f(bb')-f(b)f(b')$, $f(ab)-af(b)$ and $f(1)-1$ are finite sums in $C$ and reduce to zero in every $C_n$, since each $f_n$ is an $A$-algebra map. Step 2 makes each coefficient of each difference zero. Thus $f$ is an $A$-algebra map, with exactly the prescribed reductions.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Theorem B.3.2(1), formula (B.3.1), printed p.288; agent proof of its split-source completion calculation, using only affine duality and the Noetherian maximal condition.

proof.text: For each $b$, $\Delta_C f(b)-(f\otimes f)\Delta_B(b)$ is an element of $C\otimes_AC$, identified with the free $A$-module on $M^2$ by the two inverse coefficient maps of Step 3. It is a finite sum, and its reduction modulo every $\mathfrak m^n$ vanishes by the comultiplication identity for $f_n$. Thus it is zero by Step 2. The element $\epsilon_C f(b)-\epsilon_B(b)\in A$ and the finite sum $s_C f(b)-f(s_B(b))\in C$ likewise reduce to zero for every $n$, so vanish. Consequently $f$ respects all three operations. The affine homomorphism bijection of Step 1 gives a group homomorphism $u:D_A(M)\to G$. The explicit tensor identification there shows that the coordinate map of its reduction is $f_n$, so its reduction is the specified $u_n$, rather than just an isomorphic homomorphism.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Theorem B.3.2(1), formula (B.3.1), printed p.288; agent proof of its split-source completion calculation, using only affine duality and the Noetherian maximal condition.

proof.text: If $u,v:D_A(M)\to G$ have identical reductions, their coordinate maps send each $b\in B$ to finite sums whose difference has every coefficient in $\bigcap_{n\geq1}\mathfrak m^n=0$, by injectivity of the completion map. The coordinate maps coincide, and affine duality gives $u=v$. Conversely reductions of any group homomorphism form a compatible family by functoriality of affine base change. Steps 5--6 give a preimage of every such family, and this argument gives its uniqueness. This is the claimed bijection. In particular the proof does not impose smoothness; it allows torsion in $M$, including in the residue characteristic, and the trivial group $M=0$.
